answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by tying every vote to collateral locked in a vault. An attacker who splits one stake among a hundred fake names gains nothing, because each name must post its own bond; with quadratic pricing ten voices cost a hundred times one. Honest agents travel the same voyage and grow trust slowly, like a lotus unfolding, while a forger must pay for every petal of a false identity. The cost of swelling a mob therefore outruns any benefit from it.
